title: P versus NP: Computation as Counting

rows.label: A1
rows.predicate: $\NPC$-completeness and self-reducibility: satisfiability is $\NPC$-complete (Cook, Levin), the reductions reach combinatorial mathematics (Karp), and polynomial time is invariant across the standard machines (Church--Turing).

rows.label: A2
rows.predicate: Proof complexity, used as proved: $\NPC=\coNP$ iff some propositional proof system is polynomially bounded (Cook--Reckhow); Extended Frege is not automatizable unless RSA breaks, bounded-depth Frege unless factoring and Diffie--Hellman are feasible, and resolution is $\NPC$-hard to automate.

rows.label: A3
rows.predicate: One-way functions and the average case: the discrete logarithm and factoring as the canonical instances (Diffie--Hellman), Impagliazzo's worlds; Shor's order finding, which inverts both for a quantum observer.

rows.label: A4
rows.predicate: The three barriers: relativization (Baker--Gill--Solovay), natural proofs (Razborov--Rudich), algebrization (Aaronson--Wigderson); Wigderson's survey of what a separation must use.

rows.label: A5
rows.predicate: Eckmann and Tlusty: under uniform angle scaling a single walk in $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ reaches the identity only on a measure-zero set, while the doubled walk returns for some exponentially large scaling, delivered non-constructively.

rows.label: A6
rows.predicate: The corpus: the horizon clause and its complexity face (00:Z1--Z4; 25:G3, 25:G7), the shell theorem (00:Z10; 20:E1, 20:E12), the scale import $\Om=4S+1$ (00:A7), the window ladder $P^{2}<\Om$ (00:B8), the four generative levels (00:B6), the drive of every prime shell (00:A12).

blocks.title: Computation as counting along a representation

rows.label: B1
rows.predicate: A representation $R=(E_R,O_R,c_R)$: an encoding, a finite set of elementary operations, and the cost, the graph distance in $G_R$. $R$ is admissible when it and a standard machine simulate each other with polynomial overhead. Cost is counted in bit operations, $\ell=\log_2P$ for a carrier element and $n$ for a stored length-$n$ object.

rows.label: B2
rows.predicate: Cost is a function of the pair (target, representation), not of the target alone: a target far in one chart can be near in another, and the transform between charts is itself a path. ``Within the horizon'' is a predicate on pairs.

rows.label: B3
rows.source: Prop.~\ref{prop:longturn}; A6\newline \pywit{pnp}{p26009}{B3}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p26009}{B3} \lean{FRC.Horizon.shift\_power\_character, FRC.Horizon.eigenphase, FRC.Shell.Frame.pow\_inj, FRC.Horizon.shift\_trace, FRC.Ladder.eigenvalues13}

rows.label: B4
rows.predicate: The continuum reading [chart]: the dilation generator $\HH=-\mathrm i(x\partial_x+\tfrac12)$ has $x^{-1/2+\mathrm i\nu}$ as eigenfunction of eigenvalue $\nu$ on $x>0$, so the frequency index is the spectrum of $\HH$ in the chart of the scale shift (20:E1).

rows.label: B5
rows.predicate:
The Gauss sum couples the two turns: multiplication by a unit permutes the units; $\sum_{t
eq0}\psi(tc)$ is $-1$ for $c
eq0$ and $P-1$ for $c=0$; $\sum_u\chi(u)=0$ for $\chi
eq1$; hence $\lvert g(\chi)vert^{2}=P$ for every nontrivial $\chi$ on the shell ($\Om$ on the Carrier).
rows.source: Rem.~\ref{rem:gauss}; B3\newline \pywit{pnp}{p26011}{B5}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p26011}{B5}, \leanwit{FrcLedger}{p26011}{B5} \lean{FRC.Horizon.ramanujan\_sum, FRC.Horizon.ramanujan\_zero, FRC.Shell.Frame.principal\_root, FRC.Ladder.mul\_perm, Pnp.gauss\_product, Pnp.gauss\_modulus}

rows.label: C1
rows.predicate: Two horizons, nested: the per-instance feasible horizon $H(\ell)$, polynomial in the feasible regime, and the absolute horizon $\Om^{1/4}$, the observer's total budget in the totality. The totality holds the inverse of every ascent whole, the table of $P-1$ index pairs, below its own count: the endpoint-given oracle.

rows.label: C2
rows.predicate: The family's size and the table beyond the horizon [chart]: at the anchor $2^{204}<\sqrt\Om<2^{205}$, so the shells of the family $P^{2}<\Om$ have at most $205$ bits; $2^{102}<\Om^{1/4}<2^{103}$, so a decision table with one entry per $204$-bit input exceeds the absolute horizon and lies below $\sqrt\Om$.

blocks.title: Proof as a bounded path; certificate as a near-representation

rows.label: D1
rows.predicate: The classes in a representation: $L\in\PC_R$ when a $\mathrm{poly}(\ell)$ uniform rule selects each next operation and the deterministic forward path reaches the decision bit within $H(\ell)$; $L\in\NPC_R$ when a certificate of polynomial length places ``accept'' within $H(\ell)$ of $(E_R(x),w)$. The axis is find versus exist.

rows.label: D2
rows.predicate: Faithfulness: for every admissible $R$, $\PC_R=\PC$ and $\NPC_R=\NPC$. The forward direction simulates each operation in polynomial time and guesses the operation sequence with the certificate; the reverse rewrites a standard computation as an $R$-derivation of polynomial length.

rows.label: D3
rows.predicate: The classes are representation-invariant; what varies with $R$ is the cost of a specific target within a fixed budget. A certificate is a representation in which the far target is near: supplied ($\NPC$) rather than forward-constructed ($\PC$).

rows.label: D4
rows.predicate: Faithfulness is to the class structure on the carrier family: the carrier classes are $\PC$ and $\NPC$, the textbook asymptotic classes their degenerate idealisation. No tower of carriers is admitted; a fixed length admits a decision table, decided by the totality, unreachable below the horizon (C2).

blocks.title: P versus NP: finding versus checking

rows.label: E1
rows.predicate: The search problem $\mathrm{Search}_V$ of $L\in\NPC$ with verifier $V$ and witness bound $p$ maps an instance to a witness or to $\bot$. The near-representation is forward-constructible iff $\mathrm{Search}_V\in\mathrm{FP}$.

rows.label: E2
rows.predicate: The crisp form: $\PC=\NPC$ iff $\mathrm{Search}_V\in\mathrm{FP}$ for every $L\in\NPC$, equivalently for $\mathrm{SAT}$; by self-reduction on the variables and the witness-preserving Cook--Levin reduction.

rows.label: E3
rows.predicate: A propositional proof system is a polynomial-time onto map $\Pi$ to $\mathrm{TAUT}$; $p$-bounded when every tautology has a polynomial-size proof; automatizable when some algorithm finds a proof in time polynomial in the tautology and its least proof size.

rows.label: E4
rows.predicate: The witness--automatization dictionary: for $L\in\NPC$ with verifier $V$, $\mathrm{Search}_V\in\mathrm{FP}$ iff the certificate system $\Pi_V$ (a witness system, not a system for $\mathrm{TAUT}$) is automatizable; so $\PC=\NPC$ iff every witness system is automatizable.

rows.label: E5
rows.predicate: Finding collapses to checking: if $\PC=\NPC$ then every propositional proof system is automatizable, the proof built bit by bit by self-reduction on the predicate ``$\tau$ has a $\Pi$-proof of size at most $s$''.

rows.label: E6
rows.predicate: The gap is finding versus existing: the truth-table system is automatizable but not $p$-bounded, so existence ($\NPC=\coNP$) and discovery are distinct; the known separations condition the gap on the hardness of factoring and the discrete logarithm, the substrate's descent.

rows.label: E7
rows.predicate: A localizing chart for $x\in L$: an admissible chart in which some witness lies within the polynomial horizon of $\mathbf0$. A constructive localising selector emits, in $\mathrm{FP}$, such a chart with a canonical forward rule whose orbit reaches the witness in $\mathrm{poly}(\ell)$ steps. Proximity alone is insufficient.

rows.label: E8
rows.predicate: Existence is free: for every witness index $m$ of the scale chart the translation $j\mapsto j+(n-m)+1$ of the index cycle is a chart (a bijection of the cycle) that places $g^{m}$ one counting step from the origin, $g=g^{0}\cdot g$. The witness enters only to name the chart.

rows.label: E9
rows.predicate: The selector is the content: a constructive localising selector for every $L\in\NPC$, equivalently for $\mathrm{SAT}$, exists iff $\PC=\NPC$; a selector for a single easy $L$ does not suffice.

rows.label: E10
rows.predicate: The counting distance of a unit along the orbit of $g$ is its index: $m\mapsto g^{m}$ is a bijection of the index cycle onto the units, the distances $1,\dots,P-1$ have mean $P/2$ and maximum $P-1$, between $2^{\ell-1}$ and $2^{\ell}$ for $\ell$ the bit length.
rows.source: Rem.~\ref{rem:lucky}; A6\newline \pywit{pnp}{p26027}{E10}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p26027}{E10} \lean{FRC.Shell.Prime.exists\_drive, FRC.Shell.Prime.primitive\_pow\_inj, FRC.Shell.Frame.generates, FRC.Ladder.two\_mul\_distSum, FRC.Ladder.dist\_le, FRC.Ladder.bits\_bracket}

rows.label: E11
rows.predicate: Three quantities differ: the naive orbit length (up to $2^{\ell}$ steps), the cost of a specified algorithm (baby-step--giant-step, F3), and the minimum complexity of the descent, the open lower bound. The bijection of E10 bounds none of them. Short to name is not short to find.

blocks.title: The directional asymmetry is a one-way function

rows.label: F1
rows.predicate: Charts and the family: on $\F_P$ the additive chart and the scale chart $(\F_P^{\times},\cdot)\simeq C_{P-1}$; with a fixed generator $g$ the ascent $a_P(j)=g^{j}$ and the descent $d_P=\mathrm{dlog}_g$. The carrier family is $\{\F_P:P^{2}<\Om\}$ (00:B8), input size $\ell$, feasibility $\mathrm{poly}(\ell)$.

rows.label: F2
rows.predicate: Ascent is feasible: square-and-multiply computes $g^{j}$ in at most $2\,\mathrm{bits}(j)$ modular multiplications, hence at most $2\ell$ for $j<P$; on the three carriers $17$, $26$, $38$ multiplications at $j=P/3$, right to left with the last squaring skipped [data].

rows.label: F3
rows.predicate: The descent's count: with $m^{2}\ge P-1$ baby steps $1,g,\dots,g^{m-1}$ ($m$ entries, one multiplication per step) and at most $m$ giant steps, baby-step--giant-step recovers from $g^{x}$ an index $y$ with $g^{y}=g^{x}$; at most $2m$ operations, $m=\lfloor\sqrt{P-1}\rfloor+1$; $134$, $1334$, $13334$ on the three carriers [data].

rows.label: F4
rows.predicate: Three scales: the feasibility budget $\mathrm{poly}(\ell)$, exceeded by the descent; the per-instance descent $2\sqrt P$, at most $\Om^{1/4}$ on the family, superpolynomial yet far below carrier scale; the uniform statement that no $\mathrm{poly}(\ell)$ inverse exists across the family, with no per-instance witness.

rows.label: F5
rows.predicate: A one-way family: each $f_\ell$ computable in $\mathrm{poly}(\ell)$ while every $\mathrm{poly}(\ell)$-time inverter succeeds on at most a sub-horizon fraction of the carrier, the finite-totality reading of negligibility.

rows.label: F6
rows.predicate: One-way implies separation: if a one-way family exists then $\PC\neq\NPC$, since inverting $f$ is the search problem of the verifier $[f(x)=y]$, which $\PC=\NPC$ would place in $\mathrm{FP}$.

rows.label: F7
rows.predicate: The scale-descent residue: the ascent family $\{a_P\}$ on the carrier family is one-way, $\mathrm{poly}(\ell)$ forward and inverted by no $\mathrm{poly}(\ell)$ forward computation. Decided by the totality, beyond the bounded observer; the complexity literature posits the same statement as the discrete-logarithm hardness assumption (00:Z4).

rows.label: F8
rows.predicate: If the scale descent is one-way (F7) then $\PC\neq\NPC$.

rows.label: F9
rows.predicate: The native locus: ascent is a horizon-bounded forward count, descent its inverse below the horizon; $\PC\neq\NPC$ follows from F7 one way, the converse not known. The single arrow of the drive is the structural reason for the residue, the descent the time-reversed branch a composed observer cannot freely take.

rows.label: F10
rows.predicate: The descent is the inverse coordinate map: $a_P:j\mapsto g^{j}$ is the bijection of $C_{P-1}$ onto $\F_P^{\times}$ carrying the time index to its position, and $d_P=\mathrm{dlog}$ its inverse, a cyclic-group coordinate, not the inverse of the multiplicative Fourier transform (B3).

rows.label: F11
rows.predicate: The scaling flow returns the doubled walk: Eckmann and Tlusty's two facts (A5) read on the shell as the find--exist split, a designated point unreachable by the single scaling, the relaxed target met non-constructively at an exponential scaling. A geometric parallel, not a lower bound.

rows.label: G1
rows.predicate: The four primitive roles on $\F_P$ with the generator $g$: succession $x+1$, addition $x+a$, multiplication $mx$, fixed-base exponentiation $a_P(j)=g^{j}$, each the previous iterated with a fixed operand; the fourth is the top, its inverse the discrete logarithm.

rows.label: G2
rows.predicate: Ladder closure: the four roles generate the two cyclic structures, $C_P$ additive and $C_{P-1}$ multiplicative, with the bridge $a_P$. A tower exponent $g^{j}$ is read modulo $P-1$, so tetration is exponentiation of a reduced index, and the power map acts on the index as multiplication; no third cyclic structure hosts a fifth role (00:B6).
rows.source: Prop.~\ref{prop:closure}; A6, G1, G3\newline \pywit{pnp}{p26041}{G2}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p26041}{G2} \lean{FRC.Shell.Frame.pow\_mod, FRC.Ladder.tower\_reduces, FRC.Ladder.power\_index, FRC.Ladder.tower13}

rows.label: G3
rows.predicate: Phase-index dynamics: in the scale chart $x=g^{m}$ the power map acts by $P_k(g^{m})=g^{km}$ and its iterates by $P_k^{\,r}(g^{m})=g^{k^{r}m}$, the exponents read modulo $P-1$; the ascent is the orbit traversal $g^{j+1}=g\cdot g^{j}$, one multiplication per counted step.

rows.label: G4
rows.predicate: The one-way function is the inverse of the last role: each forward role costs one modular operation, the ascent at most $2\ell$ multiplications; the descent recovers the index, the position in the counted orbit of the fourth role. The descent/ascent operation ratio at the three carriers is $134/17$, $1334/26$, $13334/38$ [data].
rows.source: Prop.~\ref{prop:invlast}; F2, F3, G3\newline \pywit{pnp}{p26043}{G4}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p26043}{G4} \lean{FRC.Ladder.sqmul\_count\_of\_lt\_pow, FRC.Ladder.bsgs\_spec, FRC.Ladder.ascent\_step}

rows.label: G5
rows.predicate: The power map $P_k$ is a bijection of $\F_P^{\times}$ iff $k$ is invertible modulo $P-1$, inverted by $x\mapsto x^{a}$ with $ak\equiv1$; otherwise its image is the cycle of $g^{d}$, $d=\gcd(k,P-1)$, of exactly $(P-1)/d$ elements.
rows.source: Rem.~\ref{rem:closuretransform}; G3\newline \pywit{pnp}{p26044}{G5}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p26044}{G5} \lean{FRC.Ladder.power\_bijective\_of\_unit, FRC.Ladder.power\_image, FRC.Ladder.power\_image\_index, FRC.Ladder.compressive\_of\_gcd, FRC.Ladder.powers13}

rows.label: G6
rows.predicate: The index cycle $C_{P-1}$ is the abelian hidden-subgroup datum on which Shor's transform acts, the chart H5 marks as the hard classical case. The one-way map is the exponential $a_P$, whose inverse is the discrete logarithm, not the power map, which is efficiently inverted when bijective (G5).

rows.label: H1
rows.predicate: The two quarter turns as a structured correspondence: the transverse turn (the additive transform) is forward-computable classically on a stored vector; the longitudinal turn's period is reached by a $\BQP$ observer through order finding, not by reading a transform vector. A correspondence between charts and the observers that reach them, not a complexity theorem.

rows.label: H2
rows.predicate: A chart change $T$ is forward-computable when $T$ and $T^{-1}$ lie in $\PC$; a problem is transform-diagonalisable by $T$ when its instances become pointwise in the $T$-chart. Well defined for abelian and hidden-subgroup problems, not a feature of $\NPC$ at large.

rows.label: H3
rows.predicate: Fourier-diagonalisable implies $\PC$: the additive transform on the shell is exact and self-inverse, $T^{-1}T=1$ on the full cycle $n=P-1$ (the round trips on the sub-cycles $n=8$, $256$, $2^{16}$ over $\F_{17}$, $\F_{257}$, $\F_{65537}$ [data]); the cyclic convolution costs $n^{2}$ multiplications in the position chart and $\tfrac32n\log_2n+n$ through the transform ($1\,048\,576$ against $16\,384$ at $n=2^{10}$) [data].

rows.label: H4
rows.predicate: Structured witness sets are forward-localizable: when the witnesses of $x$ are the solutions of an affine $\F_2$-system readable from $x$, Gaussian elimination returns a particular solution $w_0$ and a basis; the chart $w\mapsto w-w_0$ places $w_0$ at $\mathbf0$ and every solution within the basis's size in counting steps.

rows.label: H5
rows.predicate: The scale chart is the hard case: the discrete logarithm is the carrier's native order-finding instance, reached by a $\BQP$ observer and, under F7, by no classical forward computation; factoring is a distinct instance not covered by F7. A correspondence on structured instances, not a boundary theorem.

rows.label: J1
rows.predicate: A universal constructive selector would invert the one-way family: applied to the inversion family of a one-way $f$ it inverts $f$ in $\mathrm{poly}(\ell)$; under F7 none exists, and its non-existence is equivalent to $\PC\neq\NPC$ (E9). The natural-proofs reading is an analogy, the density not established.

rows.label: J2
rows.predicate: The barriers as obstructions: relativization treats the shell as a featureless sphere, natural proofs forbid a large generic marking where the hardness is the non-generic alignment with the arrow, algebrization adds an algebraic oracle the carrier's scale arithmetic replaces. The reading is a locus, not a technique the barriers exclude.

blocks.title: The horizon clause and the residue

rows.label: K1
rows.predicate: $\Om$-hard: a statement the totality decides and whose instance witnesses are checkable at sub-carrier scale, while its uniform forward-findable certificate is carrier-scale, below the bounded observer's horizon. Decidable, not undecidable: settled at the scale of the whole (00:Z3).

rows.label: K2
rows.predicate: The three faces: the shell theorem's classical screen value in 20-rh (every mode on the self-dual line; classical RH as the count equality, $\Om$-hard in its uniform form), the uniform per-$n$ Goldbach bound, and the forward-invertibility of the scale descent are one horizon clause, decided by the totality beyond the bounded observer (00:Z2).

rows.label: K3
rows.predicate: Frequency and the spectrum [chart]: the frequency chart is the spectrum of the scale shift on the shell (B3), the dilation generator its continuum reading (B4, 20:E1). The Hilbert--P\'olya correspondence is a target of 20-rh, not a result; the spectral and the computational faces meet on the one $\HH$-axis as a reading.

rows.label: K4
rows.predicate: An arrow-forward computation: a $\mathrm{poly}(\ell)$-length path applying only the drive-forward operations of the carrier.

rows.label: K5
rows.predicate: Why the single arrow stops short of a proof: forbidding the inverse outright is circular; admitting every $\mathrm{poly}(\ell)$ operation makes the exclusion $\mathrm{dlog}\notin\mathrm{FP}$, which implies $\PC\neq\NPC$ one way; the closure removes the circularity (G4) and leaves the lower bound as the residue.

rows.label: K6
rows.predicate: The irreducible residue: the uniform certificate that the inverse of the last role has no $\mathrm{poly}(\ell)$ forward algorithm across the carrier family, the computational face of the horizon clause, decided by the totality and below the bounded observer's horizon (00:Z4).

B3.name: FRC.Horizon.shift_power_character
B3.doc: 20:E1, 20:E12, 26:B3 — the power characters are eigenvectors of the scale-shift `x ↦ g^r x` in the `𝔽_p` reading: `(g^r x)^k = (g^r)^k · x^k`.

B3.name: FRC.Horizon.eigenphase
B3.doc: 20:E12 (iii), 20:Z10, 26:B3 — the eigenvalue `(g^r)^k` of the mode `k` under the scale-shift is a `(p − 1)`-th root of unity, independent of the vector.

B3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.pow_inj
B3.doc: 26:B3 — the powers `g⁰, …, g^{n−1}` of the drive are distinct: `g^i = g^j` with `i, j < n` forces `i = j`.

B3.name: FRC.Horizon.shift_trace
B3.doc: 20:E12, 20:E1, 26:B3 — clause (iii) in the `𝔽_p` reading: the fixed-point count of the scale-shift, the trace of its permutation matrix: `x ↦ g^r x` fixes every nonzero residue when `(p − 1) ∣ r` and none otherwise, `Tr S^r = (p − 1)·[(p − 1) ∣ r]`; the shell's trace carries no prime data.

B3.name: FRC.Ladder.eigenvalues13
B3.doc: 26:B3, the reference shape — the twelve eigenvalues `2^ν` of the scale shift on `𝔽₁₃` are distinct.

B5.name: FRC.Horizon.ramanujan_sum
B5.doc: 20:B7, 26:B5 — the flat ground state: in a shell `𝔽_q` with a frame (no zero divisors) and an element `ω` of order exactly `m`, the Ramanujan sum `Σ_{a=1}^{m−1} ω^{an}` equals `−1` for every `n ≢ 0 (mod m)`. With `m = p` this is `c_p(n) ≡ −1`: the mode at the spectral origin carries no prime information.

B5.name: FRC.Horizon.ramanujan_zero
B5.doc: 26:B5 — the Ramanujan sum at `n = 0`: `Σ_{a=1}^{m−1} ω^{0·a} = m − 1` (the additive character sum over the units is `P − 1` for `c = 0`, against `−1` for `c ≠ 0`); no hypothesis on `ω`.

B5.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.principal_root
B5.doc: 2:F1 (Prop. 6.1), 26:B5, 26:H3 — `g` is a principal root of unity: `g^n = 1`, `Σ_{j<n} (g^k)^j = 0` for `0 < k < n`, and `n = p − 1` reads as `−1` in the shell.

B5.name: FRC.Ladder.mul_perm
B5.doc: 26:B5 — multiplication by a unit `c` is injective on the shell and reaches every residue.

B5.name: FRC.Pnp.gauss_product
B5.doc: 26:B5 — the Gauss-sum product on a finite field into any domain (`FRC.HorizonML.gauss_product`, `Theme/Horizon.lean`).

B5.name: FRC.Pnp.gauss_modulus
B5.doc: 26:B5 — the Gauss-sum modulus over the complex numbers (`FRC.Chart.gauss_modulus`, `Theme/Chart.lean`).

C2.name: FRC.Pnp.family_bits
C2.doc: 26:C2 [chart] — the family's bits and the table beyond the horizon (`FRC.Chart.family_bits`, `Theme/Chart.lean`).

E8.name: FRC.Ladder.recentre_witness
E8.doc: 26:E8 — the recentred witness sits one step from the origin: `g^{recentre m} = g = g^0 · g`.

E8.name: FRC.Ladder.recentre_inj
E8.doc: 26:E8 — the recentring is a chart: a bijection of the index cycle (injective on the `n` indices).

E8.name: FRC.Ladder.recentre_surj
E8.doc: 26:E8 — the recentring reaches every index `j < n` (from `i = (j + m + n − 1) % n`): with `recentre_inj`, a bijection of the index cycle.

E8.name: FRC.Ladder.recentre13
E8.doc: 26:E8, the reference shape — every index of `𝔽₁₃` is recentred to one step from the origin.

E10.name: FRC.Shell.Prime.exists_drive
E10.doc: 00:A12, 26:E10, 26:F10 — every prime carries a frame: the prime shell `𝔽_p` has a drive `g`, a primitive root of order `p − 1`, and its powers `g^m`, `m < p − 1`, reach every nonzero residue (`⟨g⟩ = 𝔽_p^×`, the pigeonhole).

E10.name: FRC.Shell.Prime.primitive_pow_inj
E10.doc: 26:E10, 26:F10 — the powers `g⁰, …, g^{p−2}` of a primitive root are distinct.

E10.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.generates
E10.doc: 00:A12, 26:E10, 26:F10 — the drive generates: every nonzero residue is a power `g^m`, `m < p − 1` (the pigeonhole).

E10.name: FRC.Ladder.two_mul_distSum
E10.doc: 26:E10 — the distances `1, …, n` have mean `(n + 1)/2` (`P/2` on the cycle of `n = P − 1` units): `2 · Σ_{k<n} (k + 1) = n (n + 1)`.

E10.name: FRC.Ladder.dist_le
E10.doc: 26:E10 — the maximum of the distances `1, …, n` is `n`: every `k + 1` with `k < n` is at most `n`.

E10.name: FRC.Ladder.bits_bracket
E10.doc: 26:E10 — the bit-length bracket: `2^(ℓ−1) ≤ e < 2^ℓ` for `ℓ = bits e`, `e > 0`.

F2.name: FRC.Ladder.sqmul_count
F2.doc: 26:F2, 26:G4 — square-and-multiply uses at most `2·bits e` multiplications; for `e < 2^l`, at most `2l`.

F2.name: FRC.Ladder.sqmul_count_of_lt_pow
F2.doc: 26:F2, 26:G4 — for an exponent below `2^l`, square-and-multiply uses at most `2l` multiplications: `O(ℓ)` on a shell of `ℓ` bits.

F2.name: FRC.Ladder.sqmul13
F2.doc: 26:F2, the reference shape — square-and-multiply on `𝔽₁₃` computes every `2^e`, `e < 64`, within `2·bits e` multiplications; `2^{11}` in seven.

F3.name: FRC.Ladder.bsgs_spec
F3.doc: 26:F3, 26:G4 — the descent: for `m ≤ n ≤ m²`, baby-step–giant-step from `h = g^x` (`x < n`) returns `(i, j)` with `g^{j + m i} = h`, so the index is recovered modulo `n`, after at most `m` giant-step multiplications.

F3.name: FRC.Ladder.bsgs_total
F3.doc: 26:F3 — the descent's total: the `m` baby steps and the giant multiplications together are at most `2m`.

F3.name: FRC.Ladder.baby_step
F3.doc: 26:F3 — the baby steps are one multiplication each: `g^{j+1} = g^j · g`.

F3.name: FRC.Ladder.descendsB_spec
F3.doc: 26:F3 — the kernel's verdict unpacked: when `descendsB` holds, the search returns `(i, j)` with `j < m` and `g^{j + m i} = h`.

F3.name: FRC.Ladder.descent13_101
F3.doc: 26:F3, the reference shape and `𝔽₁₀₁` — baby-step–giant-step recovers every index: on `𝔽₁₃` with `m = 4` (`16 ≥ 12`), on `𝔽₁₀₁` with `m = 10` (`100 ≥ 100`), the pair returned reconstructs the target.

F10.name: FRC.Shell.Prime.exists_drive
F10.doc: 00:A12, 26:E10, 26:F10 — every prime carries a frame: the prime shell `𝔽_p` has a drive `g`, a primitive root of order `p − 1`, and its powers `g^m`, `m < p − 1`, reach every nonzero residue (`⟨g⟩ = 𝔽_p^×`, the pigeonhole).

F10.name: FRC.Shell.Prime.primitive_pow_inj
F10.doc: 26:E10, 26:F10 — the powers `g⁰, …, g^{p−2}` of a primitive root are distinct.

F10.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.generates
F10.doc: 00:A12, 26:E10, 26:F10 — the drive generates: every nonzero residue is a power `g^m`, `m < p − 1` (the pigeonhole).

G2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.pow_mod
G2.doc: 26:G2 — powers of the drive are periodic with period `p − 1`.

G2.name: FRC.Ladder.tower_reduces
G2.doc: 26:G2 — a tower exponent is read modulo `n`: `g^{(g^j)} = g^{(g^j) mod n}`; tetration is exponentiation of a reduced index, and the two cyclic structures host every iterate.

G2.name: FRC.Ladder.power_index
G2.doc: 26:G2, 26:G3 — the power map on the index: `(g^m)^k = g^{km mod n}`, multiplication by `k` on the index cycle.

G2.name: FRC.Ladder.tower13
G2.doc: 26:G2, the reference shape — a tower exponent is read modulo `12`: `2^{(2^j)} = 2^{(2^j) mod 12}` on `𝔽₁₃`.

G3.name: FRC.Ladder.power_index
G3.doc: 26:G2, 26:G3 — the power map on the index: `(g^m)^k = g^{km mod n}`, multiplication by `k` on the index cycle.

G3.name: FRC.Ladder.phase_index
G3.doc: 26:G3 — the iterated power map on the index: `P_k^r(g^m) = g^{k^r m mod n}`.

G3.name: FRC.Ladder.ascent_step
G3.doc: 26:G3, 26:G4 — the ascent is counting along the orbit: `g^{j+1} = g^j · g`, one multiplication per step.

G3.name: FRC.Ladder.phase13
G3.doc: 26:G3, the reference shape — the phase formula on `𝔽₁₃`: two iterates of `x ↦ x³` carry `2^m` to `2^{9m mod 12}`, and three iterates of `x ↦ x²` to `2^{8m mod 12}`.

G4.name: FRC.Ladder.sqmul_count_of_lt_pow
G4.doc: 26:F2, 26:G4 — for an exponent below `2^l`, square-and-multiply uses at most `2l` multiplications: `O(ℓ)` on a shell of `ℓ` bits.

G4.name: FRC.Ladder.bsgs_spec
G4.doc: 26:F3, 26:G4 — the descent: for `m ≤ n ≤ m²`, baby-step–giant-step from `h = g^x` (`x < n`) returns `(i, j)` with `g^{j + m i} = h`, so the index is recovered modulo `n`, after at most `m` giant-step multiplications.

G4.name: FRC.Ladder.ascent_step
G4.doc: 26:G3, 26:G4 — the ascent is counting along the orbit: `g^{j+1} = g^j · g`, one multiplication per step.

G5.name: FRC.Ladder.power_bijective_of_unit
G5.doc: 26:G5 — when `ak ≡ 1 (mod n)` the power map `x ↦ x^k` is a bijection of the units, inverted by `x ↦ x^a`.

G5.name: FRC.Ladder.power_image
G5.doc: 26:G5 — when `d ∣ k`, `n = d·e` and `ak = bn + d` (the gcd as a Bezout witness), the image of the power map `x ↦ x^k` on the units is the cycle of `g^d`: every value is a power of `g^d`, every power of `g^d` is a value, and the powers `(g^d)^i`, `i < e`, are distinct — the image has exactly `e = n/d` elements.

G5.name: FRC.Ladder.power_image_index
G5.doc: 26:G5 — the compressive image has at most `e = n/d` elements: every value of `x ↦ x^k` is `(g^d)^i` with `i < e` (with `power_image`'s distinctness of those powers, exactly `e`).

G5.name: FRC.Ladder.compressive_of_gcd
G5.doc: 26:G5 — the only-if: when `d = gcd(k, n) > 1` the image has fewer than `n` elements (`e < d·e = n`), so the power map is no bijection of the units.

G5.name: FRC.Ladder.powers13
G5.doc: 26:G5, the reference shape — on `𝔽₁₃` the power map `x ↦ x⁵` is a bijection (`5 · 5 = 25 ≡ 1 (mod 12)`), and `x ↦ x⁴` compresses the units onto the three powers of `2⁴ = 3` (`gcd(4, 12) = 4`, `1 · 4 = 0 · 12 + 4`).

H3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.dft_inverse
H3.doc: 2:F3 (Prop. 6.3), 6:B5, 26:H3 — the inversion of the shell Fourier matrix, entrywise: with `W k j = g^{jk}` and `W' l j = −g^{(n−j)l}` (`= −g^{−lj}`), `Σ_{l<n} W k l · W' l j = [k = j]`. The matrix `g^{jk}` on the full cycle `n = p − 1` is both the longitudinal character table (26:B3) and the additive transform on the shell (26:H3).

H3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.principal_root
H3.doc: 2:F1 (Prop. 6.1), 26:B5, 26:H3 — `g` is a principal root of unity: `g^n = 1`, `Σ_{j<n} (g^k)^j = 0` for `0 < k < n`, and `n = p − 1` reads as `−1` in the shell.
